title: Bitsbox Alternatives: 5 Coding Options Like Bitsbox - Cratejoy
summary: Compare five coding picks like Bitsbox for kids 6 to 12, from typed-code games to a STEM box in the mail, by age, price, and commitment.
body_markdown:
## The alternatives


Typed code, one game at a time


### CodeMonkey vs Bitsbox


[See CodeMonkey’s home plans on codemonkey.com →](https://www.codemonkey.com/parents/)


**Best for:** An 8- to 12-year-old who liked the typing part of Bitsbox best and wants each lesson to feel like a level to beat.


CodeMonkey is an online course where kids write code to solve game-style puzzles, then build games of their own. Its first text course, Coding Adventure, is for ages 8 to 12 and has kids typing code from the first challenge to help a monkey catch bananas. Python courses follow in middle school, and younger kids start with block puzzles.


#### What feels familiar


Coding Adventure uses CoffeeScript, which CodeMonkey describes as similar to JavaScript, the language Bitsbox teaches. A parent account shows each kid’s progress and finished projects, the job the Grownup Guide does for Bitsbox.


#### What changes


Nothing arrives in the mail, and there are no cards to collect. Plans bill every three months or once a year, not monthly. It’s the least expensive pick here, and a Family plan covers three kids.


A box in the mail every month


### STEM Discovery Boxes vs Bitsbox

**Best for:** A 7- to 12-year-old whose favorite part of Bitsbox is the box itself, and who would trade typed code for wires, motors, and experiments.


Three projects arrive each month for ages 7 through the teen years. Coding is on the seller’s list of topics, next to electronics, chemistry, physics, and hydraulics.


#### What feels familiar


Mail that’s just for the kid, every month, with every supply for its projects inside, so there’s nothing to gather before starting.


#### What changes


The past boxes on the listing are builds and experiments, like a wiggling drawing robot, a solar-powered fan, and circuits made from conductive dough. None of them is a typed-code project. A 12-month prepay brings the price to $30 a box.


Siblings, or a beginner not ready to type


### Tynker vs Bitsbox


[See Tynker on tynker.com →](https://www.tynker.com/)


**Best for:** A family with two or three kids at different levels, including a 5- or 6-year-old who can’t type code yet.


Tynker starts kids on drag-and-drop blocks, with picture-based coding for kids who can’t read yet, then moves them into typed JavaScript and Python. Courses run from game design to Minecraft mods, and a placement test chooses where each kid begins.


#### What feels familiar


Bitsbox is built so siblings can share one subscription, each with a coding account. Tynker plans cover up to three kids, and typed JavaScript is waiting once a kid moves past blocks.


#### What changes


Tynker bills by the quarter, by the year, or once for lifetime access, with a 30-day money-back guarantee. Blocks come before typing for most new coders, and nothing ships.


Month to month, with a teacher to ask


### CodaKid vs Bitsbox


[See CodaKid’s self-paced plan on codakid.com →](https://codakid.com/self-paced-online-coding-classes/)


**Best for:** An 8-and-up kid who wants to make Minecraft mods or Roblox games, in a family that wants to be able to stop any month.


CodaKid’s self-paced plan opens more than 100 video courses taught by professional software developers. JavaScript and Scratch courses start at age 6, Minecraft and Roblox at 8, and Python at 10.


#### What feels familiar


JavaScript is on the menu from age 6, and help is close by. CodaKid’s teacher team answers questions from inside the course, much like the coding support in Bitsbox Premium.


#### What changes


Lessons are videos on a screen, with nothing in the mail. Most of CodaKid’s course tracks start at age 8 or older, so it fits the upper end of Bitsbox’s range best.


Ages 12 and up, ready for hardware


### TechCrate Pro vs Bitsbox


[See TechCrate Pro on protechtrader.com →](https://www.protechtrader.com/techcrate-pro)


**Best for:** A Bitsbox graduate, 12 or older, who wants code that makes a real circuit light up, move, or sense the room.


ProTechTrader’s TechCrate Pro mails a programmable board every month, such as an Arduino-compatible, an ESP32, or a Raspberry Pi Pico, with three to five sensors or modules. Guides cover C++ in the Arduino IDE and MicroPython.


#### What feels familiar


Like Bitsbox, it comes every month with step-by-step projects and code a kid types, then changes to see what happens.


#### What changes


It’s built for 12 and up and adds wiring to the coding. TechCrate Pro is a new tier, with no reviews on its page yet.
